experiment: Retail LI_ELITE PBR roughness and metallic surface maps in the Basic PBR shader, isolated against identical scalar-only PBR values

scene.camera: fixed LookAtCamera at (0,0,7), looking at origin
scene.lighting: two identical directional lights facing the front hull and black ambient
scene.control: PBR remains active with the same scalar factors; map references are removed for scalar-only, then roughness, metallic, or both references are restored independently.

linear_channel_evidence.shader: PBR.frag.hlsl getRoughness/getMetallic sample .r and multiply the scalar factor; the diffuse albedo alone uses SRGBtoLinear.
linear_channel_evidence.OpenGL_format: ATI1 DDS maps load as SurfaceFormat.Rgtc1 and GL_COMPRESSED_RED_RGTC1_EXT, a linear single-channel format.

interpretation: Both real NAP BC4 maps are loaded into the production LI_ELITE retail mesh PBR path. Independent removal of each map changes rendered pixels while keeping the PBR shader and scalar factors fixed. This proves the shader consumes each R channel and the OpenGL upload is linear. This run used UV0 for both maps (uv=0 and pbr_uv=0); the independent pbr_uv selector is now implemented and covered by parser/resolver tests, but its UV1 GPU effect and the independent UV animation case remain unverified.
